cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift to the station. Which am I doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you leave dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. It won't stir the gravy. Do I finish their dinner or drive you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finish dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose again: suitcase downstairs now, or gravy without lumps for your parents?

mechanism: A makes resolving competing immediate duties a pupil priority exercise and refuses solutions that quietly add another simultaneous job.
confusable: Not simple inability to help: each response requires B to choose the priority and own its consequence.
comparison: Kitchen/lift conflict narrowed to suitcase versus collection route narrowed to communication delay.
seedUse: Use D34 gravy/timer/taxi/suitcase chain; S05 grading choice explains why A presses B to choose again.
